alignments.note: Third-person imperative; the supplied English imperative auxiliary *Let* rides with the lexical verb *count* under rules 7 and 9, discontinuously under rule 15. Head on the lexical verb per rule 17.
Correlative quantifier rendered by the three-word English frame *as many as*; head on the quantity word *many* under rule 17, the framing *as* words being the idiom's supplied parts.
Copula of the relative clause.
Predicate noun; ASV *servants* (marginal gloss: bondservants).
Preposition.
Anarthrous Greek noun; the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun it determines, per rule 51's anarthrous clause, since no Greek article competes.

Article governing an expressed head noun with the possessive adjective ἰδίους standing attributively between them; rule 47 gives the supplied possessive to the adjective and empties the article under rule 20.
Rule 47: ἴδιος carries the supplied possessive *their own*, headed on *own*, the word realizing the lexeme.
Head noun, left bare by rule 47.
Predicate adjective.
Quantifier.
Anarthrous genitive; no article stands to anchor a determiner, so the case preposition *of* stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause. Discontinuous under rule 15.
Purpose conjunction realized by the English complementizer *that* under rule 40.
Article to *the* under rule 19.
Noun.
Article before θεοῦ with no English determiner written; rule 23.
The case preposition *of* stays with the noun, the article having no determiner to anchor it (rules 21, 23).
Conjunction.
Article to *the*.
Noun.
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*; no negative indefinite stands, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Passive subjunctive; the auxiliary *be* rides with the lexical participle under rule 9, headed on *blasphemed*. Discontinuous around *not* under rule 15.

review_notes: The imperative auxiliary *Let* is kept inside ἡγείσθωσαν's unit rather than split off as its own token, per rule 73's refusal to head a bare *let* on itself and rule 17's refusal of a word chosen merely because it is finite.
ζυγόν and τιμῆς are both anarthrous, so their supplied determiner and case preposition are rule 7/21 helpers on the nouns themselves.
